newsitem.title: USA: H&R Block still planning Compuserve spinoff.
newsitem.headline: H&R Block still planning Compuserve spinoff.

text.p: Tax preparer H&R Block Inc. still plans to spin off its remaining 80 percent interest in CompuServe Corp., possibly before the struggling online service returns to profitability, CompuServe's chairman said Friday.
Chairman Frank Salizzoni, speaking with reporters after Columbus, Ohio-based CompuServe's annual meeting, declined to forecast when CompuServe might return to profitability.
He also said the No. 2 online service would consider selling the company if any offers emerge.
"If there is somebody out there that is interested, then obviously we have to consider strategic alternatives like that," Salizzoni said. He did not say he was putting the company up for sale.
CompuServe's corporate services unit has performed well, but its consumer online service -- second to America Online Inc. -- has struggled.
Salizzoni said it would not make sense to create two separate companies from the units because both use CompuServe's network, which he said is one of the company's strengths.

Columbus, Ohio-based CompuServe lost $101.9 million, or $1.10 a share, in the nine-month period ending Jan. 31, compared with a profit of $50.2 million, or 68 cents a share, in the year-earlier period.
Kansas City, Mo.-based H&R Block spun off one-fifth of the company in an initial public offering last April but postponed selling the rest in August.
"We wanted to stabilise the financial situation, get the trends moving in the right direction (and) increase the cash position, which we're doing," Salizzoni said.

CompuServe's loss of $14.2 million, or 15 cents a share, for the fiscal third quarter ended Jan. 31 was narrower than its second-quarter loss of $58 million, or 63 cents a share, and the company showed positive cash flow.

Salizzoni said he had interviewed one candidate for the chief executive post vacated last month by Robert Massey. Salizzoni, who is acting CEO, declined to say when someone might be chosen for the job.
He repeated the online provider's view that a lawsuit filed against it this week by Time Warner Inc.'s Time magazine over its two-year contract with CompuServe was without merit.
Time is suing the online service in a federal court in Ohio for at least $3.5 million for seeking to eliminate the magazine from its online service.
CompuServe, founded in 1969 and the oldest major online service, has 3.2 million subscribers excluding its Japanese joint venture, NiftyServe. America Online has about 8 million subscribers.
